draft.title: Reconciliation and the churches
card: Many Aboriginal children were removed from their families under government policies. Churches ran some of the missions and homes that took part, so some churches played a part in the removals.
Since then, many churches have publicly apologised for their role in removing Aboriginal children. An apology admits that harm was done and that the church was involved.
Reconciliation means building respect and a fair relationship between Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and other Australians. Many churches say they support it.
Churches may show this support by listening to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, backing recognition of their spiritual connection to land, and speaking out on justice issues.
draft.remember: Many churches have apologised for their part in removing children, and they support reconciliation.

a.q: Why have many churches apologised to Aboriginal peoples?
opts: They admit their part in removing Aboriginal children
They were ordered by courts to pay for land claims
They wanted to convert more Aboriginal people
They had set the removal policies for governments
a.why: Churches ran some missions and homes involved in removing children, and the apologies admit that role. The policies were government policies, so saying churches set them is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what some missions and homes did.

b.q: A church in Newcastle holds a service where its leaders say sorry for past removals and then join a local Aboriginal-led reconciliation group. What does this show?
opts: An apology paired with support for reconciliation
An apology that replaces the need for reconciliation
Support for reconciliation without admitting any harm
A government program run by the church
b.why: The leaders admit past harm by apologising and then act to build a fair relationship by joining the group. The apology does not replace reconciliation, because reconciliation is an ongoing relationship that the church is continuing to build.
b.clue: The church does two things: it says sorry and it takes part.

a.best: They admit their part in removing Aboriginal children

b.best: An apology paired with support for reconciliation

problems.detail: The clue 'The church does two things: it says sorry and it takes part' almost restates the right option ('An apology paired with support for reconciliation'). A student can match it without understanding reconciliation.
